headline_en: Bribe-taking video on Facebook, election officer transferred
summary_en: A Bahrain-based expatriate filmed himself paying a bribe to the Goalanda upazila election officer in Rajbari for a new national ID card and posted it on Facebook; the officer was transferred to Jhenaidah on 16 Sep 2026 while an inquiry continues. The article reports allegations that a broker ring working through local computer shops takes BDT 5,000 to over half a lakh per NID job, and quotes an unnamed person who paid BDT 50,000 for a voter ID to go abroad urgently.

facts.statement: On 10 Sep 2026 Bahrain expatriate Russell Molla of Ujanchar, Goalanda upazila, Rajbari went to the Goalanda Upazila Election Office for a new voter ID (NID) card; upazila election officer Khabirul Alam demanded a BDT 5,000 bribe for the work and, after much pleading, Russell paid BDT 2,000.

Russell Molla, a Bahrain expatriate ill with a brain tumour, said the Goalanda election officer made him come back to the office for three to four days on various excuses and issued his national ID card only after he paid; he secretly filmed the payment and posted it on Facebook.

After the bribe video spread on social media, Goalanda upazila election officer Khabirul Alam was show-caused by the district election officer (reply due in three working days, submitted 15 Sep 2026) and then transferred to the Jhenaidah District Election Office by a notification signed on 16 Sep 2026 by Election Commission Secretariat assistant secretary Mohammad Shahidur Rahman; further action may follow after the inquiry.
facts.source_in_article: Rajbari district election officer (name printed both as Sek Mohammad Jalalur Rahman and Sek Muhammad Jalal Uddin)

facts.statement: It is alleged that several local computer shopkeepers in Goalanda, Rajbari are part of a broker ring: money handed to them reaches the election officer at once, and new NID cards, corrections of name spelling and corrections of father's and mother's names then get done very easily. The alleged bribe per job ranges from a minimum of BDT 5,000 to more than half a lakh taka.

An unnamed person said he paid BDT 50,000 to get a voter ID made at the Goalanda Upazila Election Office because he needed to go abroad urgently, and that nobody in that office does any work without money.
Khabirul Alam told Prothom Alo that an inquiry against him is under way and he cannot comment.

headline_en: How much economic and diplomatic gain if Bangladesh joins the Mecca alliance
summary_en: An opinion column by a Shahjalal University professor on the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan joint defence pact signed in Mecca on 7 Aug 2026 and whether Bangladesh should join. It argues the biggest potential benefit is the Saudi labour market, citing BMET figures for 2025, but says such gains need separate labour agreements, skills programmes and effective consular management.

facts.statement: According to the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET), about 1,117,000 (11 lakh 17 thousand) Bangladeshis went abroad for employment in 2025, of whom more than 752,000 (7 lakh 52 thousand) went to Saudi Arabia.
facts.source_in_article: BMET data, cited by the columnist from BSS (2026)

facts.statement: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca on 7 Aug 2026 (the 'Mecca Pact'); at the first committee meeting in Istanbul on 31 Aug 2026 it was named the 'Mecca Defence Alliance', with a permanent secretariat in Riyadh and a Pakistani representative as first secretary general for three years.
facts.source_in_article: Turkish foreign minister Hakan Fidan, as cited by the columnist

facts.statement: Bangladesh's participation in the Mecca Defence Alliance is not decided: Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman told parliament the government would consider it positively if members want to include Bangladesh, State Minister Humayun Kabir said Bangladesh sees no risk in joining, and no formal invitation or membership terms have been publicly confirmed.

The columnist argues closer political ties with Saudi Arabia could let Bangladesh press Riyadh on opening new sectors for skilled workers, transparency in recruitment, preventing contract breaches, ensuring wages and working conditions and more legal aid for expatriate workers, but that joining a defence framework will not guarantee these; separate labour agreements, skills development programmes and effective consular management are needed.
facts.source_in_article: columnist Dr Md Shahabul Haque, professor, Political Studies, SUST Sylhet

facts.statement: International media reported that on 9 Aug 2026 Yemen's Houthis attacked an Aramco facility in the Jazan area of Saudi Arabia.
facts.source_in_article: international media, cited by the columnist

summary_en: A reader-contributed report on an 'Ekphrasis' festival of dance, poetry, film and photography by migrant workers held on 30 Aug 2026 at The Salon hall of the National Museum of Singapore. A short film by Bangladeshi migrant Mainul Islam depicted poor catering food for workers and warned about online scams that empty migrant workers' bank accounts.

facts.statement: An 'Ekphrasis' festival centred on migrant workers' lives was held on 30 Aug 2026 at 'The Salon' hall of the National Museum of Singapore, with dance by the group 'Nioba Age' (as transliterated), poetry on the theme 'Our Favourite Haunts' by Bangladeshi migrant poet Belal Hasan, Indonesian poets Ade Rayani and Udiya Retnowati and Filipino poet Christine Alcabasa, a photo exhibition by migrant workers, and Singaporean host Jay Ong.

The Bangla short film 'Rajar Agomon' by Bangladeshi migrant Mainul Islam, screened with English subtitles in Singapore, warns migrant workers to beware of online scams in which fraudsters trap simple workers and take the money from their bank accounts, and tells them to follow all Singapore government rules.
facts.source_in_article: the film, as described by the contributor

facts.statement: The film 'Rajar Agomon' portrays the poor quality of catered food supplied to migrant workers in Singapore, which the report says matches migrant workers' real lives exactly.

headline_en: Highly educated young people fight for a single peon's job
summary_en: An opinion column by a Prothom Alo editorial assistant on youth unemployment in Bangladesh, using two reports of graduates competing for low-grade government posts. It says young people pay BDT 20-25 lakh on 'body contract' to cross the Mediterranean and drown, die from Ukrainian drones, and that 8-9 lakh must go abroad each year, many by selling homesteads and borrowing at high interest through brokers.

facts.statement: The columnist writes that Bangladeshi young people are drowning while trying to cross the Mediterranean on 'body contract' deals costing BDT 20-25 lakh, and that young men are dying one after another from Ukrainian drone strikes.

According to the columnist, 22-23 lakh young people join Bangladesh's labour market each year, at most 12-13 lakh find work in the country (about 3 lakh of them in decently paid government and private jobs), and 8-9 lakh young people have to go abroad each year in search of work.

The columnist writes that those who can go abroad legally are the lucky ones; a large share sell their homestead, borrow at high interest and go through brokers, and many who go by illegal routes are forced into a slave-like life. He adds that spending on education abroad is now almost equal to the higher-education budget.
The 2022 census counted about 4 crore 59 lakh people aged 15-29 in Bangladesh, about 28 percent of the population.

In Pabna, 17 of those appointed to 18 office-assistant (grade 20, formerly MLSS/peon, class-eight qualification) posts advertised on 25 Oct 2025 were highly educated; and 1,234,409 people applied for 312 third-class (grade 16, HSC-level) posts at the Department of Social Services, 3,956 per post.
facts.source_in_article: two Prothom Alo reports cited by the columnist

headline_en: Bangladesh far more exposed on energy and remittances
summary_en: At the Bengal Delta Conference 2026 in Dhaka on 24 Jul 2026, Chinese researcher Jin Liangxiang of the Shanghai Institute of International Studies said Bangladesh is highly exposed to the Iran war crisis because it imports energy from the Gulf and has a very large number of workers in GCC countries who could lose their jobs if those economies fall into serious crisis. The rest of the report covers a Stimson Center fellow's remarks on Myanmar and the Rohingya.

facts.statement: Jin Liangxiang, director of Middle East Studies and senior fellow at the Shanghai Institute of International Studies (SIIS), said that if the economies of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries fall into serious crisis over time because of the Iran war, the large number of Bangladeshi expatriate workers there could lose their jobs; their remittances play a special role in keeping Bangladesh's economy running.
facts.source_in_article: Jin Liangxiang, speaking at the Bengal Delta Conference 2026, Dhaka

facts.statement: Jin Liangxiang said disruption to fuel oil supply and higher international oil prices from the Iran war are already visible, that the Iran war could have a bigger global impact than the Ukraine war, that Iran is significantly self-reliant militarily and able to sustain a long conflict, and that Bangladesh must be prepared for any situation and act to reduce potential losses.
The two-day international 'Bengal Delta Conference 2026' in Dhaka was organised by the research body Dhaka Institute of Research and Analytics (DAIRA); the first day was Friday 24 Jul 2026.

headline_en: Three members of a Bangladeshi family killed in Italy, mourning at the Noakhali home
summary_en: Three members of a Bangladeshi family from Companiganj, Noakhali, Kamal Uddin alias Babul (39), his wife Arzu Akter (38) and daughter Arisha (5), were hacked to death at their home in the Casalotti area of western Rome at about 9 pm local time on 26 Jun 2026; son Ayon (20) is in hospital. The motive and attackers are unknown. Kamal went to Italy in 2009 and took his family there in 2024.

facts.statement: At about 9 pm local time on Friday 26 Jun 2026 in the Casalotti area of western Rome, Italy, Kamal Uddin alias Babul (39), son of Sirajul Islam of Charkakra union, Companiganj, Noakhali, his wife Arzu Akter (38) and daughter Arisha (5) were killed with sharp weapons at home; his son Ayon (20) was seriously injured and is being treated in a Rome hospital.

Relatives in Italy said several attackers followed Kamal Uddin into his home as he returned from work and hacked him, his wife and children; a neighbour who heard screams found the three bodies, and law enforcement visited the scene. The family has no specific information on the motive or who was involved.

facts.statement: Kamal Uddin went to Italy in 2009, came to Bangladesh in 2024 and took his family to Italy, and last visited Bangladesh in 2025 ('last year').
Companiganj police station OC Md Nurul Hakim said a police team was sent to the victims' village home; UNO Md Masudur Rahman said the upazila administration assigned a person to gather details.

headline_en: Masud Uddin Chowdhury on four-day remand in ACC case
summary_en: A Dhaka court on 21 Jun 2026 granted four days' remand of former MP Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury in an Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) case alleging embezzlement of over BDT 119 crore in the name of sending workers to Malaysia. The remand petition says the government-set fee was BDT 78,990 but he and others, appointed as agents through abuse of official power, illegally collected BDT 119 crore 32 lakh 70 thousand from workers and laundered it.

facts.statement: According to the ACC's remand petition, the government-fixed fee for sending a worker to Malaysia was BDT 78,990.

On Sunday 21 Jun 2026 special judge Md Sabbir Foyez of the Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Judge Court granted four days' remand (seven sought by investigating officer ACC assistant director Abul Kalam Azad) of former MP Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury in an ACC case over alleged embezzlement of more than BDT 119 crore in the name of sending workers to Malaysia.

The ACC alleges that Masud Uddin Chowdhury and associated persons, in collusion and by abusing government power, got themselves appointed as agents for sending workers to Malaysia and illegally collected BDT 119 crore 32 lakh 70 thousand from workers, which was then laundered through illegal transfer, conversion and transactions; the case is under the Penal Code, the Money Laundering Prevention Act and the Prevention of Corruption Act.

Masud Uddin Chowdhury was arrested in the Baridhara area of Dhaka on 23 Mar 2026, has been taken on remand several times in various cases (including a human trafficking case, per a linked headline) and has been in jail since.

Masud Uddin Chowdhury was GOC of the army's 9th Division in 2007 and a key figure in the 1/11 changeover, became High Commissioner to Australia in 2008, later ran restaurants and other businesses in Dhaka, and was Jatiya Party MP for Feni-3 (Sonagazi-Daganbhuiyan) in 2018 and 2024.

facts.statement: Gias Uddin Shikdar (60) of Uttar Alamnagar village, ward 1, Charbhadrasan Sadar union, Charbhadrasan, Faridpur, who had gone to Saudi Arabia about three and a half years earlier and worked on an agricultural farm under an owner in the Al-Jouf area, was hit by a speeding vehicle from the opposite direction while crossing the road on his way home from work at about 3:30 pm on Wednesday 17 Jun 2026; a doctor declared him dead at hospital.

headline_en: Two from Jamalpur killed in drone strikes after going to war for Russia
summary_en: Two men from Madarganj, Jamalpur, Mafol Mia (24) and Md Arif Mia (30), were killed in separate Ukrainian drone strikes while fighting for the Russian army; families confirmed this on 15 Jun 2026. Both went to Russia in April 2026 through a broker on the promise of mason or good work but were handed to the Russian army. The deaths were at first concealed and the families learned through a Bangladeshi expatriate in Russia.

facts.statement: Arif Mia had a job in Bangladesh's Ansar force and left it to go to Russia; those who took him promised good work but took him to Russia and handed him over to the country's army, and he was then forced to go to war, according to a local UP member.

headline_en: 'Education loans' for medical and dental students; loans also for higher study abroad
summary_en: Presenting the FY2026-27 budget in parliament on 11 Jun 2026, Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury proposed education loans for medical and dental students and a special bank loan programme for meritorious students going abroad for higher study. For migrant workers he announced continuing and expanding Probashi Kallyan Bank loans of up to BDT 10 lakh, 'Bangladesh Support Centres' at embassies in labour-market countries, reintegration programmes for returnees and easier repatriation of bodies, and said migration processing is fully digital through the Overseas Employment Platform (OEP).

facts.statement: The FY2026-27 budget announced that loans of up to BDT 10 lakh on easy terms for expatriate workers through Probashi Kallyan Bank will continue and the programme's scope will be widened.
facts.source_in_article: Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, budget speech

facts.statement: The budget speech said 'Bangladesh Support Centres' will be set up at Bangladesh embassies in countries Bangladesh depends on for its labour market; through them workers who are in jail, abused or cheated will be rescued, new employment will be found, and legal aid will be given in disputes with employers.

The budget speech said programmes will be taken for rehabilitation and social protection of expatriates who return home, and an initiative will be taken to simplify the process of bringing home the bodies of Bangladeshi workers who die abroad.
The government said the migration process has already been made fully digital through the Overseas Employment Platform (OEP).
facts.source_in_article: government, in the FY2026-27 budget speech

facts.statement: The finance minister proposed a special bank loan programme for meritorious students going abroad for higher education, alongside education loans for medical and dental students, so that financial limits do not block a meritorious student's higher study; the article gives no amounts or terms.
facts.source_in_article: Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury

facts.statement: The proposed FY2026-27 budget is BDT 9 lakh 38 thousand crore with a revenue target of BDT 6 lakh 95 thousand crore.

headline_en: The 3 proposals from UK universities to stop visa fraud
summary_en: The Russell Group of 24 leading UK universities called for targeted, risk-based action against student visa fraud rather than blanket restrictions, after the UK government announced a stricter compliance regime for universities sponsoring student visas. It proposed giving universities access to UKVI fraud data, considering penalties harsher than the current 10-year re-entry ban, and a direct fraud-reporting channel, and listed checks members already make on applicants' qualifications, English test results and financial documents.

facts.statement: The current penalty for a fraudulent UK student visa application is a 10-year re-entry ban; the Russell Group has proposed that the UK consider harsher punishment than this.
The UK government recently announced a stricter compliance regime for universities that sponsor student visas; the article gives no details of the measures.

Russell Group universities say they already apply these checks to international applicants: an extra approval step before issuing the CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies), mandatory second-person review of applications, verifying academic qualifications directly with the awarding institution, verifying English language test results with the test provider, and checking financial documents through banks and third-party verification.

The Russell Group's other two proposals are to give universities direct access to UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) data on forged documents, regional trends and recruitment agents' conduct, and to open a direct fraud-reporting channel between universities and UKVI with clear rules for sharing information on suspect applicants.

Russell Group chief executive Professor Libby Hackett said attempts to get student visas by fraud and false information undermine trust in the whole system and put genuine students' opportunities at risk; the group says the vast majority of international applicants are genuine and most international students leave the UK within five years of arrival, and it opposes blanket restrictions.

headline_en: Madaripur youth killed after going to war on Russia's side
summary_en: Suruj Kazi (35) of Madaripur Sadar was killed while fighting for the Russian army against Ukraine; the family confirmed it on 21 May 2026. He first tried for Europe through a broker, failed to get a visa, went to Russia through an agency eight months earlier for ordinary work, and ended up in the Russian army through a Bangladeshi broker. The family demands the body be brought home; police say they will investigate if a complaint is filed.

facts.statement: Suruj Kazi (35), son of Shahabuddin Kazi of Dakshin Khagrachhara, Madaripur Sadar, was killed while fighting against Ukraine for the Russian army; the article says he was killed in an enemy attack on Monday and elsewhere that he died in a mine explosion. His family confirmed the death on the evening of Thursday 21 May 2026.

Suruj Kazi decided to go to Europe through a Bangladeshi broker; after failing to get a European visa despite many attempts he went to Russia through an agency (unnamed) eight months before his death. He was supposed to join normal work there but fell into the hands of a Bangladeshi broker and joined the Russian army.
Suruj Kazi's death in the Russian army was at first kept secret; two young Bangladeshi expatriates in Russia informed his family by mobile phone.

Madaripur Sadar UNO Wadia Shabab said that if the family makes contact, help will be given to bring the body home; Madaripur Sadar Model police station OC Abul Kalam Azad said police have no information on how he joined the Russian army and will investigate and take legal action if the family files a complaint.
facts.source_in_article: UNO Wadia Shabab; OC Abul Kalam Azad

facts.statement: Suruj Kazi was the eldest of three brothers and a sister; his only child, a two-year-old son, died of a cold-related illness three months before him, leaving wife Sumaiya Akter (22). His father asked the government to bring the body home and help the family.

headline_en: 'I heard after my son died that he had gone to war; had I known I would not have let him go to Russia'
summary_en: Abdur Rahim (30) of Fulbaria, Mymensingh went to Russia on 7 Dec 2024 for about BDT 5 lakh as a welder, later took BDT 3 lakh more from his family for a supposed power-plant job, and in fact joined the Russian army through a broker on a promise of high pay. After a month's training he joined on 1 May 2026 and was killed by a drone the next day, his first day at the front, together with Riyad Rashid of Kishoreganj; campmate Limon Dutta of Narsingdi was injured. The family wants the broker tried and the body returned.

facts.statement: Abdur Rahim (30) of Putijana Namapara village, Putijana union, Fulbaria, Mymensingh went to Russia on 7 Dec 2024 spending about BDT 5 lakh; the family understood he was doing welding work there.
Three months before his death Abdur Rahim took a further BDT 3 lakh from his family saying it was for a new job at a power plant in Russia; it later emerged he was in Russian army training.

Abdur Rahim told his younger brother that the 'new company' would pay BDT 2 lakh a month and that all problems would be solved in two months; in the month before his death he sent home BDT 1 lakh 40 thousand, which surprised the family. After reaching Russia he had earlier sent money only irregularly.

Abdur Rahim's mother said he went to Russia for welding work, and a broker then took him into the army with a promise of good pay; he told his parents he had taken a power-plant job and did not say it was the army. For a month after joining the 'new job' he did not speak directly with his parents, citing network problems, but stayed in touch with two younger brothers on WhatsApp.

After one month of Russian army training Abdur Rahim joined duty on 1 May 2026 and was killed in a drone strike the next day, his first day taking part in the Ukraine war; Riyad Rashid, a young man from Kishoreganj, was killed with him and campmate Limon Dutta of Narsingdi was injured in the same attack. The family got the news on the evening of Monday 11 May 2026.
facts.source_in_article: family; Limon Dutta via Riyad Rashid's family

facts.statement: The family learned of the death because Limon Dutta, a friend in the same Russian army camp, contacted the family of Riyad Rashid by Facebook Messenger and said Rahim had also been killed; Rahim's family confirmed it through Riyad's family and Limon Dutta.

Local MP Kamrul Hasan, who visited the home with UNO Shahidul Islam and Fulbaria OC Rashedul Hasan on 12 May 2026, said he had spoken with the ministry concerned, that there is a process for bringing a body home and the family has been told to apply accordingly; the UNO promised help to bring the body quickly, humanitarian aid, and awareness work against broker rings.
facts.source_in_article: MP Kamrul Hasan; UNO Shahidul Islam

facts.statement: Abdur Rahim had earlier gone to Singapore in 2015 with money from loans and mortgaging land and worked there as a welder for seven years before returning to Bangladesh.

facts.statement: Opposition leader and Jamaat-e-Islami ameer Shafiqur Rahman said that despite missions, high commissions and embassies abroad, Bangladeshi expatriates suffer: when they go to renew passports they fall into brokers' hands and are harassed, and when someone loses a job for a fair or unfair reason nobody stands beside them.

headline_en: What are the new challenges of building public trust and stability
summary_en: An opinion column by a North South University academic arguing that Bangladesh needs professional strategic, risk and crisis communication in three sensitive areas: energy, migration and the macroeconomy. On migration it says the state's contact with migrant workers has been limited to recruitment, paperwork and formal praise, and proposes a 24-hour crisis platform, location-based SMS alerts, verified safe-area information and clear emergency-help instructions for expatriate workers.

facts.statement: The columnist recommends that the Bangladesh government set up, for expatriate workers, a separate 24-hour crisis platform, location-based SMS alerts, verified information on safe areas and clear instructions on getting emergency help, saying this would leave expatriates less panicked, less cheated and less likely to return home chaotically. These are proposals, not existing services.
facts.source_in_article: columnist Rizwan-ul-Alam, associate professor and chair, Media, Communication and Journalism, North South University

facts.statement: The columnist warns that when tension rises in a region an information vacuum becomes very dangerous and is quickly filled by broker rings, rumour-spreading groups and opportunists, so risk and crisis communication to migrants must be direct, digital and continuous.

The columnist says the state's communication with migrant workers has mostly been limited to recruitment, paperwork and formal praise, which is no longer enough amid regional conflict, labour-market uncertainty and growing rumours; expatriates must be assured, with visible arrangements, that the government has contingency plans, diplomatic contact, emergency assistance and security measures ready in a crisis.

key_quote_bn: যখন কোনো অঞ্চলে উত্তেজনা বাড়ে, তখন তথ্যের শূন্যস্থান খুব বিপজ্জনক হয়ে ওঠে। সে শূন্যতায় দ্রুত ঢুকে পড়ে দালাল চক্র, গুজব ছড়ানো গোষ্ঠী এবং সুযোগসন্ধানী পক্ষ।

headline_en: 'Everyone consoles us, nobody says when they will bring my sister back'

The assistant director of the Faridpur District Employment and Manpower Office said that after a dead worker's body is brought to Bangladesh the government sends it home by free ambulance service, gives BDT 35,000 for burial and gives BDT 3 lakh as compensation.

headline_en: Went to Saudi Arabia through a broker; after death in an accident, doubt over bringing the body back
summary_en: Azgar Bepari (38) of Dohar, Dhaka went to Saudi Arabia three and a half years ago through a broker on borrowed money and, because of visa complications, had worked illegally for a year as a welder's helper. He fell while working on a building in Riyadh on 24 Mar 2026 and died in hospital on 30 Mar. With no valid papers and no money, the family, who have heard it costs BDT 4 lakh, doubt they can bring the body home; the UNO says the Riyadh embassy arranges it with government help if contacted.

facts.statement: Azgar Bepari (38) of Radhanagar, Dohar upazila, Dhaka slipped and fell while working on a building in 'Hara' town of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia on 24 Mar 2026 (the article's opening says he fell from a roof), suffering a serious head injury; local Bangladeshi expatriates took him to 'Aziz Abdullah Hospital' in Riyadh, where he died on Monday at about 6:30 pm Bangladesh time.

Azgar Bepari went to Saudi Arabia three and a half years earlier through a broker on borrowed money; because of visa complications he had been working illegally for a year as a welder's assistant. His sister-in-law said he could not send money home for lack of work and twice deposited money for an iqama (residence permit) but did not get it; he could not come home because the loan was unpaid.
The family of Azgar Bepari, who died undocumented in Riyadh, said they are hearing from various sources that bringing the body to Bangladesh will cost BDT 4 lakh, which they cannot afford.
Dohar UNO Md Maidul Islam said the Bangladesh embassy is in Riyadh, and if it is contacted on behalf of the deceased it will arrange to send the body home with government assistance.

headline_en: 22 migrants die off the Greek coast, four of them from Sunamganj
summary_en: Four men from Derai upazila, Sunamganj died in the Mediterranean while travelling from Libya to Greece in a rubber boat; families were told on Saturday 28 Mar 2026 by another man from the same upazila who was on the boat. They died of lack of food and water and their bodies were thrown into the sea. The headline gives a total of 22 migrant deaths off the Greek coast.

facts.statement: Four men from Derai upazila, Sunamganj, named Nuruzzaman, Sajidur, Sahan and Mujibur, died in the Mediterranean while going from Libya to Greece in a rubber boat; they died from lack of food and water and their bodies were then thrown into the sea. The headline says 22 migrants in all died off the Greek coast.
facts.source_in_article: families, informed by another passenger from the same upazila

facts.statement: The Sunamganj men were travelling by rubber boat from Libya towards Greece across the Mediterranean; families got the news on the afternoon of Saturday 28 Mar 2026 from a fellow passenger from Derai who was on the same boat.

people_cases.what_happened: Travelling from Libya to Greece in a rubber boat.

headline_en: Bangladeshis whose visas expired in Saudi Arabia can go home without a fine
summary_en: The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh announced on 23 Mar 2026 that the Saudi government is letting holders of visit, Umrah, transit and final exit visas whose visas have expired, and who could not leave on time because of the regional situation, depart without a fine by 18 April. They can go straight to an international airport with a ticket with no prior procedure; the embassy warned of serious legal trouble for those who do not leave in time.

facts.statement: The Saudi government announced a special facility under which Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia holding any type of visit visa, Umrah visa, transit visa or final exit visa whose visa has expired can leave the country without paying a fine, provided they depart by 18 April (2026).
facts.source_in_article: notice of the Bangladesh Embassy, Riyadh, issued Monday 23 Mar 2026

facts.statement: The embassy notice says the facility is for Bangladeshi nationals in Saudi Arabia whose visa validity ended on 25 February (2026) and who could not leave on time because of the regional situation; elsewhere the notice describes them as visa holders whose validity 'has passed 25 February'.

Eligible expired-visa holders in Saudi Arabia can go directly to an international airport with an air ticket and leave, without paying any fine or extending the visa and without any extra prior procedure.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh specially urged expatriates to leave Saudi Arabia by 18 April without fail, warning that those who do not leave in that time may later face serious legal complications and punishment.
